subject: air-source heat pumps
note: some models keep a COP above 1 at -25 degC outdoor air, using injection circuits that bypass the evaporator or two-stage compression. Some VRF systems hold a COP above 3 at -10 degC. This is what took air-source heat pumps into cold climates, where use had been limited to ground-source.

subject: ground heat source
note: ground temperature is stable year-round at 10-15 degC, which is why ground-source units serve both summer cooling and winter heating, and can cool without running the compressor at all (free cooling) when the ground is colder than the outside air.

subject: large-capacity air-source heat pumps
note: for air-conditioning large buildings and INDUSTRIAL COOLING PROCESSES - the brief's only industrial-specific COP. Highly efficient units can exceed 6.

subject: CO2 air-source water heater (Eco Cute)
note: first practical use in Japan in 2001; annual performance factor 3.9. Uses CO2 as the process fluid. Residential, so not on the roster.

subject: variable refrigerant flow systems
note: commercially available above 5 for mid-scale building air-conditioning; the latest air-to-air models exceed 6.

subject: electricity generation, global
note: used by the brief to argue heat pumps' emissions advantage. Table 6's own worked comparison uses 0.459 kgCO2/kWh and a 30% power generation efficiency: against a 0.95-efficient gas heater delivering 100 kWh, a heat pump at SPF 4 uses 25 kWh of electricity and emits 11.5 kg where the gas heater uses 105 kWh and emits 17.1 kg. Original: HPTCJ trial calculation, 2011 [7].
